craft_notes: Sthāyin: marvel at will's might. Device: comma→dash (unwilling stated, bending questioned); comma→colon line 2 (graced stated, yoke questioned). Rejected: 'wilt' archaism overload — kept list (already archaic register, consistent). Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: Shouldst thou not list it, Śambhu — who could crook a straw?
graced by thy list, who would shirk heaven's yoke?
l4.sanskrit_cite: tvayy anicchati kaḥ śambho śaktaḥ kubjayituṃ tṛṇam tvadicchānugṛhītas tu vahed brāhmīṃ dhuraṃ na kaḥ

reads_against.argmap: When you do not will, who is capable, O Śambhu, to bend grass?; But favoured by your will — who would not carry Brahmā's yoke? → Without your will none bends grass; with it all carry Brahmā's yoke.
c1_essence: Unwished none crooks straw; wished all shoulder Brahmā's load.
reads_against.l2: Should you not wish it, Śambhu, who could crook a straw? Graced by your wish — who would shirk Brahmā's burden?
